summary: Gull Island Light, Apostle Islands, Lake Superior: planned from 1907, first shown on a skeleton tower in 1929, closed to visitors in nesting season.

light.note: Acetylene light, commissioned 30 September 1929; white flash every ten seconds, focal plane 55 ft (LighthouseFriends). Minded by keepers from Michigan Island. The record's current Fl W 2.5s is not verified here.

structures.note: Skeleton tower topped by an acetylene light, erected at a cost of $4,752 (LighthouseFriends); described as a steel tower in a 2020 notice

staffing.note: No source dates automation. LighthouseFriends says the light was minded by the keepers from Michigan Island from 1929 (the 1917 'nonattended' and 1918 'automated' wording describe the plan, not the built light).

access.note: Closed to the public 15 May to 1 September to protect nesting birds; 500 ft seaward from shore (closure listing). Best seen by boat (LighthouseFriends).

visit.note: Tower closed; the light is best seen by boat (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard owns the light (LighthouseFriends)

wrecks.outcome: Aground in dense fog on Gull Island; bound for Washburn with coal (8,000 tons per the Washburn Times; 7,800 per LighthouseFriends); total loss per LighthouseFriends; the crew went to Michigan Island

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends dates the skeleton tower's construction and the light's commissioning to 1929 (commissioned 30 September 1929). No source in this research gives 1928.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 3.7 m (ENC) against 17.0 m (Wikidata) and 56 m (OSM). LighthouseFriends gives a focal plane of 55 feet, about 16.8 m. The story and facts use 16.8 m.

notes_for_editor: (1) Record errors: first_lit 1928 (Rowlett) should be 1929 (LighthouseFriends; see corrections). Focal height 3.7 m (ENC) is inconsistent with the 55 ft focal plane (LighthouseFriends). (2) Characteristic: record Fl W 2.5 s (OSM, ENC) and Fl W 10 s (Wikidata); LighthouseFriends gives a flash every ten seconds for 1929. The current Light List value was not read and is not verified here. (3) Range: LighthouseFriends says 'up to thirteen miles'; the record says 5 nm. Not reconciled; no range is in the facts. (4) USLHS lists 'Gull Island, Minor Aid to Navigation, est. 1908': 1908 is the survey year, not the light's first lighting, and the USLHS roster is empty. (5) Tonnage of the Thomas Wilson: 8,000 tons (Washburn Times) vs 7,800 (LighthouseFriends). The newspaper says the crew went to Michigan Island and then to Bayfield; LighthouseFriends credits Keeper Edward Lane with the rescue. Not resolved. (6) The Washburn Times is dated 26 May 1921 and says the grounding was on 'Sunday'; the story says 'May 1921'. (7) Name variant: 'Edward Lane' (1921) and 'Ed Lane' (1929) in LighthouseFriends. (8) Corpus trap: the Lighthouse Service Bulletin index entries for 'Gull Island' keepers (Kendzia, Peterson; 1918-1923) refer to Little Gull Island, New York, and were not used. (9) Not read: the Lighthouse Board reports 1909-1929 (cited by LighthouseFriends and Wikipedia), the Bayfield County Press and the Duluth News Tribune of 4 October 1929; the Michigan Island keeper's log (National Archives). The Wikipedia article was read for leads only and is not cited, including its wreck list 1887-1906 and its 1943 automation date for Michigan Island. (10) No photographs added. (11) Access: the story says the tower is closed and that the island is closed in nesting season; the record's 'boat_only: true' is consistent with LighthouseFriends. (12) The record's county (Ashland) is not in any source read, so the story does not name a county. (13) LighthouseFriends' 1907 quotation of the Lighthouse Board and its 1929 log quotation are second-hand; the story footnotes them to LighthouseFriends. Fact-check 2026-10-28: (a) Keller's September 1908 recommendation is the northeast end of Michigan Island (LighthouseFriends); 'the eastern end ... is the better site' is the Commissioner's wording in the FY1915 report (scan p.93), so the 1908 event note and the story are corrected. (b) Staffing changed from 'automated' (as_of 1929) to 'unknown': no source read dates automation; LighthouseFriends says Michigan Island keepers minded the light. A human should check the Light List. (c) LighthouseFriends calls the steamer 'Captain Thomas Wilson'; the Washburn Times says 'Thomas Wilson'; the story uses the newspaper's form. LighthouseFriends' list spells 'Robert Mirland' for the Robert M. Ireland. (d) The 2020 Friends post is a blog post, not a notice; the story now says post. (e) Lane is kept on the roster with role 'other' because no Gull Island stint is recorded; the note says so. (f) Friends of the Apostle Islands (2020) calls Gull Island the smallest island in the National Lakeshore and gives its position; not used in the story.
